s: Look at the picture. A 　　　 is flying over the houses.

s: Lena doesn’t want to go 　　　 with John because she is afraid of water.

s: It is hard for trees to 　　　 along this beach because of the strong winds from the sea.

s: You may have a long drive because of the terrible 　　　.  There are usually a lot of cars and buses during this time.

s: Cindy enjoys 　　　 her dad read stories to her before bed.
e: Cindy　喜歡在睡前聽爸爸唸故事給她聽。enjoy　後面要接動名詞。

s: Mr. and Mrs. Wu have three daughters.  Two are in high school, and 　　　 is in elementary school.
e: Wu　先生和　Wu　太太有三個女兒。兩個在讀高中，另一個在讀國小。已知總共三個女兒，兩個已提及，剩下的那一個使用有限定意味的　the other。

s: Christmas 　　　 and I want to visit my aunt abroad.  Do you have any plans yet?
e: 聖誕節快到了，我想去國外看我阿姨。你已經有什麼計畫了嗎？come　為來去動詞，可用現在進行式表示未來。

s: Jo won’t be happy if you’re late for his party tonight, so 　　　 sure that you arrive on time.
e: 如果你今天晚上在　Jo　的派對遲到，他會不開心，所以要確保你能準時抵達。此句句型是　make sure that...（確保…），為祈使句，當給出指令、建議或提醒時，會省略主詞，使用原形動詞開頭。

s: I guess the rainwater has come in from the kitchen.  See?  　　　 of the windows are closed except the one in the kitchen.
e: 我猜雨水是來自廚房。你看，除了廚房那扇窗外，「全部的」窗戶都關著。(Ａ)全部(Ｂ)兩者(Ｃ)大部分(Ｄ)一些。

s: machines have been used to pick fruits for a long time, they were not used on strawberry farms until several years ago.
e: 「雖然」機器已被用來採收水果很久了，但是草莓農場直到幾年前才使用，使用表示對比關係的連接詞。(Ａ)雖然(Ｂ)因為(Ｃ)在…之前(Ｄ)如果。

s: Jane’s parents are always happy to see their grandchildren, but mine 　　　 less so when I visit them with my kids.
e: Jane　的父母總是很高興見到孫子，但我父母在我帶孩子去探訪時，就沒那麼高興。後面句子　mine　代指　my parents，是複數，而前半句話搭配的動詞為　be　動詞，故後半句動詞應搭配　be　動詞的複數形式。

s: Before she 　　　 about it, you should tell Daphne you broke her favorite cup.
e: 在她問起這件事之前，你應該告訴　Daphne，你打破了她最喜歡的杯子。句子在談及未來的計畫或行動，搭配時間連接詞，如　before / after / when / as soon as / until　時，副詞子句裡的動詞應使用現在式。

s: It was very windy this morning.  Some of the shirts on the balcony were blown away 　　　 in the pond.
e: 今天早上風很大，陽臺上的一些襯衫被風吹走，掉入池塘裡。此處使用　and　連接兩個並列動詞，時態一致，前面　were　過去式，後方應同樣使用過去式　fell，表示一個完整動作，而　fallen　是過去分詞，不能單獨當主要動詞，要和助動詞搭配使用，如　has fallen。

s: (１)　What happened to Rex?
p: Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. “Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night,” my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before!
e: 文章中的第六句提到　Rex　在醫院，而且被車撞了，可以推論　Rex　受傷了。(Ａ)牠迷路了(Ｂ)牠受傷了(Ｃ)牠咬了人(Ｄ)牠吃得太多了。

p: Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. By looking for a new home for him.

s: (１)　What is Rolling Acres?
p:
At 5 o’clock every morning, while most people are sleeping, 16-year-old Libby Larson is already up. She mops the floor, gets the mail and the newspapers, and gets ready for visitors to Rolling Acres. Libby’s grandparents started Rolling Acres in 1970, and since then all of the Larson family have been working there. Rolling Acres used to be just a sheep farm, but now, with its fruit trees, vegetable gardens, and many other kinds of animals, it has become a popular place for families to go on vacation. Visitors can pick fruits, collect eggs, and feed the animals. It is one of Libby’s jobs to show kids how to feed the baby sheep.
For her work, Libby is paid $10 an hour. This summer, she expects to make about $1,200 and plans to buy a cell phone. Her friends think it’s great to make that much money in a summer. However, for Libby, working at a family business also means making sacrifices. “I’d love to sleep until noon or go to summer camp like other kids. My friends stopped inviting me on trips because I’m always busy in the summer.” However, Libby also said, “But it’s better to see both sides. Working with your family is great. You feel closer to each other.”
e: 文章的第四句有提到，有果樹、菜園，還有許多不同種類動物的出現，它已經成為家庭度假的熱門地點。(Ａ)一座動物園(Ｂ)一個營地(Ｃ)一個度假農場(Ｄ)一個家庭餐館。

s: (３)　What does making sacrifices mean?
p:
At 5 o’clock every morning, while most people are sleeping, 16-year-old Libby Larson is already up. She mops the floor, gets the mail and the newspapers, and gets ready for visitors to Rolling Acres. Libby’s grandparents started Rolling Acres in 1970, and since then all of the Larson family have been working there. Getting to know different sides of your family.
Making excuses for failing to do something difficult.

s: (１)　What do the comics tell us?
o: Follow the old ways of life.
Save our planet before it’s too late.
Treat others the way we want to be treated.
e: 漫畫描繪復活節島的居民從擁有豐富的樹木到樹木消失殆盡，最終導致資源匱乏，警示人們過度消耗自然資源的後果。最後一格以「別讓地球，變成另一個復活節島」，呼籲人們珍惜地球。(Ａ)及時行樂(Ｂ)遵循原有的生活方式(Ｃ)在為時已晚前拯救我們的地球(Ｄ)以我們希望被對待的方式對待他人。

They fought for land and plants all the time.
They prayed to the statues beside a large fire.
They used statues to show how strong they were.

s: (３)　What does did it in Picture 7 mean?
o: Move the statues to fighting grounds.
e: 第七格說明「那些砍下最後樹木的人肯定知道樹對他們有多重要—但他們還是這麼做了（did it）」這裡的 it 指的是他們明知樹木重要卻仍然砍伐了最後樹木的這個行為。

s: (１)　What did Ariely try to find out in the origami study?
o: If he could stop the IKEA effect.
Why IKEA furniture is so famous.
If anyone shared his IKEA experience.
e: 第一段的倒數第二句說明，Ariely　在組裝完後，對自己完成的櫃子產生特別的喜愛，甚至超過其他的家具。第二段第一行說明他想知道是否也有其他人有類似的感受，因此設計了摺紙研究，並邀請兩組人「製作者」和「購買者」加入。

s: (２)　Which is true about the origami study?
o: Buyers would spend less on builders’ origami than builders would.
Builders and buyers needed to decide a price on the origami they made.
Builders knew others would not pay as much for the origami as they would.
Buyers would spend more on builders’ origami after knowing how they were made.
e: 他的研究中，「製作者」是親手摺紙的人，並在他們完成作品後，詢問他們會花多少錢買作品，而「購買者」是購買這些摺紙的人，Ariely　會把摺紙作品給他們看，並詢問他們願意支付多少錢購買。而最後的研究結果顯示，購買者願意為製作者的摺紙支付的價格（5　分錢）遠低於製作者自己認為的價值（25　分錢）。(Ｂ)並非由製作者和購買者共同決定價格。實驗的重點在於比較兩者各自的估價(Ｃ)文中第二段最後一句，製作者原本認為其他人也會願意支付和他們自己認為的相同金額(Ｄ)文章並未說明因此無法判斷。

s: (３)　Jerry just can’t get his daughter Mia to eat more vegetables at dinner.  Every time he tries to do so, there is always a lot of shouting and crying.  If Jerry wants to have Mia eat more vegetables by using the IKEA effect, what should he do?
o: Tell Mia that he cooks the vegetables just for her.
Ask Mia to help him cook vegetables for her meal.
Give Mia her favorite candy after she eats vegetables.
Ask Mia what vegetables she likes and cook them for her.
e: 「IKEA　效應」表示：人們對自己親手製作的物品會產生更高的喜愛感。因此，如果　Jerry　想讓　Mia　更喜歡吃蔬菜，他應該讓　Mia　參與準備蔬菜的過程，讓她產生「自己製作」的感覺。

s: (１)　What is the reading mainly about?
p:
In the picture is a UK electricity worker in the 1970s. Pictures like this appeared in many newspapers at the time. In 1972, electricity workers in the UK asked to be paid more, and they decided to stop working until their wish was answered. The government worried that there wouldn’t be enough electricity for the country if these workers didn’t go to work, so it agreed to give them the pay rise. However, the story didn’t end there.
　　A year later, the electricity workers asked for another pay rise. To get what they wanted, they worked shorter hours and acted like they would walk away from their job anytime. But this time, the government decided to fight. To save electricity, it made new rules for people to follow. For example, each family could turn on the heat in only one room; TV stations had to stop their shows at 10:30 p.m.; businesses could open only three days a week.
　　People’s lives were greatly changed. Without enough heat to keep the house warm, people covered themselves in blankets all the time. Hospitals had to use candles because they couldn’t keep all the lights on. Factories couldn’t keep their machines working. Many people lost their jobs. For months, people were paying the price while the electricity workers were fighting for their wish. In the end, the government agreed to the second pay rise. This picture shows what many people thought of the electricity workers during the “dark” time.
o: The tips on using a picture to tell a story.
The change that electricity brought to people’s lives.
The history behind the picture of a UK electricity worker.
The story of a famous UK electricity worker from the 1970s.
e: 先描述　1972　年英國電力工人要求加薪並罷工的事件，接著第二段講述，隔年他們再次要求加薪並採取更強硬的行動，英國進入能源短缺時期，人們的生活發生巨大的改變。最後，則以圖片敘述當時人們對電力工人的看法。故選(Ｃ)一張英國電力工人圖片背後的歷史。

s: (３)　Why does the writer put the “　” mark around the word dark in the last sentence?
p:
In the picture is a UK electricity worker in the 1970s. Pictures like this appeared in many newspapers at the time. In 1972, electricity workers in the UK asked to be paid more, and they decided to stop working until their wish was answered. The government worried that there wouldn’t be enough electricity for the country if these workers didn’t go to work, so it agreed to give them the pay rise. However, the story didn’t end there.
　　A year later, the electricity workers asked for another pay rise. To get what they wanted, they worked shorter hours and acted like they would walk away from their job anytime. But this time, the government decided to fight. To save electricity, it made new rules for people to follow. For example, each family could turn on the heat in only one room; TV stations had to stop their shows at 10:30 p.m.; businesses could open only three days a week.
　　People’s lives were greatly changed. Without enough heat to keep the house warm, people covered themselves in blankets all the time. Hospitals had to use candles because they couldn’t keep all the lights on. Factories couldn’t keep their machines working. Many people lost their jobs. For months, people were paying the price while the electricity workers were fighting for their wish. In the end, the government agreed to the second pay rise. This picture shows what many people thought of the electricity workers during the “dark” time.
o: To say that the “dark” time was actually not dark.
To tell people that the word was said by the government.
To mean both the days without lights and the difficult lives people lived.
To show that the government and the electricity workers both lost their fights.
e: 文章第三段一開始描述，因為電力工人的行動導致停電和能源短缺，使人們的生活陷入困境與巨大改變，如同處於「黑暗」之中。
